facts.statement: The genus Messelornis was described by Hesse in 1988.
Messelornis is the most abundant bird from the Messel Lagerstätte, with over 500 known specimens representing roughly half of all bird fossils from that site.
facts.quote: It is the most abundant bird from the Messel Lagerstätte, representing roughly half of all Messel bird fossils with more than 500 specimens known.

facts.statement: The fossil record of Messelornis spans from the Paleocene to the middle Eocene.
facts.quote: The fossil record of Messelornis ranges from the Paleocene to the middle Eocene.

facts.statement: Messelornis was probably not an especially adept flier.
facts.quote: It was probably not an especially adept flier.

facts.statement: Messelornis was an omnivore with a diet that included seeds, fruits, and fish.
facts.quote: It was omnivorous and had a diet including seeds, fruits, and fish.

facts.statement: The type species M. cristata was initially thought to have a comb-like crest, but this feature is now believed to be unrelated plant material.
facts.quote: The name of the type species, M. cristata, refers to the fact that it was initially interpreted as having a comb-like crest, but the existence of this crest has since been reinterpreted as unrelated plant material.

facts.statement: One of Messelornis's feathers displayed iridescent coloration, though no chemical analysis has been performed.
facts.quote: One of its feathers had an iridescent coloration, but no chemical analysis has been done yet.

facts.statement: Messelornis is classified within the order Gruiformes and is interpreted as a relative of rails.
facts.quote: Messelornis has remained a member of the Gruiformes and is now interpreted as a relative of rails.

facts.statement: Specimens of M. cristata show a distinct range of sizes that researchers think is due to sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Specimens of M. cristata display a distinct range of sizes thought to be a result of sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: M. nearctica is distinguished from M. cristata by having longer, more slender toes and a unique hypotarsus morphology.
facts.quote: M. nearctica, which is known from the Eocene Green River Formation. It is distinguished from M.cristata by its longer and more slender toes among other skeletal characteristics such as its unique hypotarsus morphology.

facts.statement: The species M. russelli is known from the Paleocene of France and is represented by two poorly preserved humeri.
facts.quote: M. russelli, which is known from the Paleocene of France and includes two humeri which are poorly preserved.

facts.statement: The parent group of Messelornis is the family Messelornithidae.
Messelornis lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)
